![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/3cba44923f4f583cf6e01ac87cdd6e5ca73a75993eef8322cd01bf44416f84f4.png)

Evaluate the triple integral 
${∭}_{R}4x\,dV$
over the region $R,$ shown above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the right one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/f112dd83a8cbb7563979dc170db23db7e178ba1762aca23fd4073c50e1c7a343.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type III region

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,0\le y\le 5-x-z\},
$$

where

$$
D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 2\}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/71974fddc8e0e0b6a12fc6a248c15eea08c9f6b8a0823d50aede8aadc31a41fa.png)

Hence, the type III representation of $R$ is

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 5-x-z\}
$$

As a result, by writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}4x\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{5-x-z}4x\,dy\,dz\,dx.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y$, treating $x$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{5-x-z}4x\,dy\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{5-x-z}4x\,dy]dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}4x[y]_{y=0}^{y=5-x-z}\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}4x(5-x-z)\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}(20x-4{x}^{2}-4xz)\,dz\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}(20x-4{x}^{2}-4xz)\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{2}(20x-4{x}^{2}-4xz)\,dz]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[20xz-4{x}^{2}z-2x{z}^{2}]}_{z=0}^{z=2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(32x-8{x}^{2})\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}(32x-8{x}^{2})\,dx & ={[16{x}^{2}-\frac{8{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =(64-\frac{64}{3})-0 \\  & =\frac{128}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
